Rom.9.24.bsb: including us, whom He has called not only from the Jews, but also from the Gentiles?
Rom.9.24.kjv: Even us, whom he hath called, not of the Jews only, but also of the Gentiles?

Rom.9.25.bsb: As He says in Hosea: “I will call them ‘My People’ who are not My people, and I will call her ‘My Beloved’ who is not My beloved,”
Rom.9.25.kjv: As he saith also in Osee, I will call them my people, which were not my people; and her beloved, which was not beloved.

Rom.9.27.bsb: Isaiah cries out concerning Israel: “Though the number of the Israelites is like the sand of the sea, only the remnant will be saved.
Rom.9.27.kjv: Esaias also crieth concerning Israel, Though the number of the children of Israel be as the sand of the sea, a remnant shall be saved:

Rom.9.28.bsb: For the Lord will carry out His sentence on the earth thoroughly and decisively.”
Rom.9.28.kjv: For he will finish the work, and cut it short in righteousness: because a short work will the Lord make upon the earth.

Rom.9.29.bsb: It is just as Isaiah foretold: “Unless the Lord of Hosts had left us descendants, we would have become like Sodom, we would have resembled Gomorrah.”
Rom.9.29.kjv: And as Esaias said before, Except the Lord of Sabaoth had left us a seed, we had been as Sodoma, and been made like unto Gomorrha.

Rom.9.30.bsb: What then will we say? That the Gentiles, who did not pursue righteousness, have obtained it, a righteousness that is by faith;
Rom.9.30.kjv: What shall we say then? That the Gentiles, which followed not after righteousness, have attained to righteousness, even the righteousness which is of faith.

Rom.11.5.bsb: In the same way, at the present time there is a remnant chosen by grace.
Rom.11.5.kjv: Even so then at this present time also there is a remnant according to the election of grace.

Rom.11.7.bsb: What then? What Israel was seeking, it failed to obtain, but the elect did. The others were hardened,
Rom.11.7.kjv: What then? Israel hath not obtained that which he seeketh for; but the election hath obtained it, and the rest were blinded

Rom.11.8.bsb: as it is written: “God gave them a spirit of stupor, eyes that could not see, and ears that could not hear, to this very day.”
Rom.11.8.kjv: (According as it is written, God hath given them the spirit of slumber, eyes that they should not see, and ears that they should not hear;) unto this day.

Rom.16.13.bsb: Greet Rufus, chosen in the Lord, and his mother, who has been a mother to me as well.
Rom.16.13.kjv: Salute Rufus chosen in the Lord, and his mother and mine.

Rom.15.12.bsb: And once more, Isaiah says: “The Root of Jesse will appear, One who will arise to rule over the Gentiles; in Him the Gentiles will put their hope.”
Rom.15.12.kjv: And again, Esaias saith, There shall be a root of Jesse, and he that shall rise to reign over the Gentiles; in him shall the Gentiles trust.

Rom.10.16.bsb: But not all of them welcomed the good news. For Isaiah says, “Lord, who has believed our message?”
Rom.10.16.kjv: But they have not all obeyed the gospel. For Esaias saith, Lord, who hath believed our report?

Rom.11.26.bsb: And so all Israel will be saved, as it is written: “The Deliverer will come from Zion; He will remove godlessness from Jacob.
Rom.11.26.kjv: And so all Israel shall be saved: as it is written, There shall come out of Sion the Deliverer, and shall turn away ungodliness from Jacob:

Rom.11.27.bsb: And this is My covenant with them when I take away their sins.”
Rom.11.27.kjv: For this is my covenant unto them, when I shall take away their sins.

Rom.1.1.bsb: Paul, a servant of Christ Jesus, called to be an apostle, and set apart for the gospel of God—
Rom.1.1.kjv: Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ, called to be an apostle, separated unto the gospel of God,

Rom.1.2.bsb: the gospel He promised beforehand through His prophets in the Holy Scriptures,
Rom.1.2.kjv: (Which he had promised afore by his prophets in the holy scriptures,)

Rom.10.17.bsb: Consequently, faith comes by hearing, and hearing by the word of Christ.
Rom.10.17.kjv: So then faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.

Rom.10.18.bsb: But I ask, did they not hear? Indeed they did: “Their voice has gone out into all the earth, their words to the ends of the world.”
Rom.10.18.kjv: But I say, Have they not heard? Yes verily, their sound went into all the earth, and their words unto the ends of the world.

Rom.10.2.bsb: For I testify about them that they are zealous for God, but not on the basis of knowledge.
Rom.10.2.kjv: For I bear them record that they have a zeal of God, but not according to knowledge.

Rom.10.5.bsb: For concerning the righteousness that is by the law, Moses writes: “The man who does these things will live by them.”
Rom.10.5.kjv: For Moses describeth the righteousness which is of the law, That the man which doeth those things shall live by them.

Rom.10.11.bsb: It is just as the Scripture says: “Anyone who believes in Him will never be put to shame.”
Rom.10.11.kjv: For the scripture saith, Whosoever believeth on him shall not be ashamed.

Rom.12.3.bsb: For by the grace given me I say to every one of you: Do not think of yourself more highly than you ought, but think of yourself with sober judgment, according to the measure of faith God has given you.
Rom.12.3.kjv: For I say, through the grace given unto me, to every man that is among you, not to think of himself more highly than he ought to think; but to think soberly, according as God hath dealt to every man the measure of faith.

Rom.12.7.bsb: if it is serving, let him serve; if it is teaching, let him teach;
Rom.12.7.kjv: Or ministry, let us wait on our ministering: or he that teacheth, on teaching;

Rom.12.11.bsb: Do not let your zeal subside; keep your spiritual fervor, serving the Lord.
Rom.12.11.kjv: Not slothful in business; fervent in spirit; serving the Lord;

Rom.12.16.bsb: Live in harmony with one another. Do not be proud, but associate with the lowly. Do not be conceited.
Rom.12.16.kjv: Be of the same mind one toward another. Mind not high things, but condescend to men of low estate. Be not wise in your own conceits.

Rom.12.17.bsb: Do not repay anyone evil for evil. Carefully consider what is right in the eyes of everybody.
Rom.12.17.kjv: Recompense to no man evil for evil. Provide things honest in the sight of all men.

Rom.12.18.bsb: If it is possible on your part, live at peace with everyone.
Rom.12.18.kjv: If it be possible, as much as lieth in you, live peaceably with all men.

Rom.12.21.bsb: Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.
Rom.12.21.kjv: Be not overcome of evil, but overcome evil with good.

Rom.6.1.bsb: What then shall we say? Shall we continue in sin so that grace may increase?
Rom.6.1.kjv: What shall we say then? Shall we continue in sin, that grace may abound?

Rom.6.12.bsb: Therefore do not let sin reign in your mortal body so that you obey its desires.
Rom.6.12.kjv: Let not sin therefore reign in your mortal body, that ye should obey it in the lusts thereof.

Rom.6.14.bsb: For sin shall not be your master, because you are not under law, but under grace.
Rom.6.14.kjv: For sin shall not have dominion over you: for ye are not under the law, but under grace.

Rom.6.18.bsb: You have been set free from sin and have become slaves to righteousness.
Rom.6.18.kjv: Being then made free from sin, ye became the servants of righteousness.

Rom.8.36.bsb: As it is written: “For Your sake we face death all day long; we are considered as sheep to be slaughtered.”
Rom.8.36.kjv: As it is written, For thy sake we are killed all the day long; we are accounted as sheep for the slaughter.

Rom.15.14.bsb: I myself am convinced, my brothers, that you yourselves are full of goodness, brimming with knowledge, and able to instruct one another.
Rom.15.14.kjv: And I myself also am persuaded of you, my brethren, that ye also are full of goodness, filled with all knowledge, able also to admonish one another.

Rom.16.19.bsb: Everyone has heard about your obedience, so I rejoice over you. But I want you to be wise about what is good and innocent about what is evil.
Rom.16.19.kjv: For your obedience is come abroad unto all men. I am glad therefore on your behalf: but yet I would have you wise unto that which is good, and simple concerning evil.

Rom.5.9.bsb: Therefore, since we have now been justified by His blood, how much more shall we be saved from wrath through Him!
Rom.5.9.kjv: Much more then, being now justified by his blood, we shall be saved from wrath through him.

Rom.5.10.bsb: For if, when we were enemies of God, we were reconciled to Him through the death of His Son, how much more, having been reconciled, shall we be saved through His life!
Rom.5.10.kjv: For if, when we were enemies, we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son, much more, being reconciled, we shall be saved by his life.

Rom.5.11.bsb: Not only that, but we also rejoice in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom we have now received reconciliation.
Rom.5.11.kjv: And not only so, but we also joy in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, by whom we have now received the atonement.

Rom.13.11.bsb: And do this, understanding the occasion. The hour has come for you to wake up from your slumber, for our salvation is nearer now than when we first believed.
Rom.13.11.kjv: And that, knowing the time, that now it is high time to awake out of sleep: for now is our salvation nearer than when we believed.

Rom.2.17.bsb: Now you, if you call yourself a Jew; if you rely on the law and boast in God;
Rom.2.17.kjv: Behold, thou art called a Jew, and restest in the law, and makest thy boast of God,

Rom.2.18.bsb: if you know His will and approve of what is superior because you are instructed by the law;
Rom.2.18.kjv: And knowest his will, and approvest the things that are more excellent, being instructed out of the law;

Rom.2.21.bsb: you, then, who teach others, do you not teach yourself? You who preach against stealing, do you steal?
Rom.2.21.kjv: Thou therefore which teachest another, teachest thou not thyself? thou that preachest a man should not steal, dost thou steal?

Rom.2.22.bsb: You who forbid adultery, do you commit adultery? You who abhor idols, do you rob temples?
Rom.2.22.kjv: Thou that sayest a man should not commit adultery, dost thou commit adultery? thou that abhorrest idols, dost thou commit sacrilege?

Rom.2.23.bsb: You who boast in the law, do you dishonor God by breaking the law?
Rom.2.23.kjv: Thou that makest thy boast of the law, through breaking the law dishonourest thou God?

Rom.5.20.bsb: The law came in so that the trespass would increase; but where sin increased, grace increased all the more,
Rom.5.20.kjv: Moreover the law entered, that the offence might abound. But where sin abounded, grace did much more abound:

Rom.14.23.bsb: But the one who has doubts is condemned if he eats, because his eating is not from faith; and everything that is not from faith is sin.
Rom.14.23.kjv: And he that doubteth is damned if he eat, because he eateth not of faith: for whatsoever is not of faith is sin.

Rom.14.19.bsb: So then, let us pursue what leads to peace and to mutual edification.
Rom.14.19.kjv: Let us therefore follow after the things which make for peace, and things wherewith one may edify another.

Rom.14.21.bsb: It is better not to eat meat or drink wine or to do anything to cause your brother to stumble.
Rom.14.21.kjv: It is good neither to eat flesh, nor to drink wine, nor any thing whereby thy brother stumbleth, or is offended, or is made weak.

Rom.16.18.bsb: For such people are not serving our Lord Christ, but their own appetites. By smooth talk and flattery they deceive the hearts of the naive.
Rom.16.18.kjv: For they that are such serve not our Lord Jesus Christ, but their own belly; and by good words and fair speeches deceive the hearts of the simple.

Rom.16.2.bsb: Welcome her in the Lord in a manner worthy of the saints, and assist her with anything she may need from you. For she has been a great help to many people, including me.
Rom.16.2.kjv: That ye receive her in the Lord, as becometh saints, and that ye assist her in whatsoever business she hath need of you: for she hath been a succourer of many, and of myself also.

Rom.16.15.bsb: Greet Philologus and Julia, Nereus and his sister, and Olympas and all the saints with them.
Rom.16.15.kjv: Salute Philologus, and Julia, Nereus, and his sister, and Olympas, and all the saints which are with them.

Rom.16.6.bsb: Greet Mary, who has worked very hard for you.
Rom.16.6.kjv: Greet Mary, who bestowed much labour on us.

Rom.3.1.bsb: What, then, is the advantage of being a Jew? Or what is the value of circumcision?
Rom.3.1.kjv: What advantage then hath the Jew? or what profit is there of circumcision?

Rom.9.6.bsb: It is not as though God’s word has failed. For not all who are descended from Israel are Israel.
Rom.9.6.kjv: Not as though the word of God hath taken none effect. For they are not all Israel, which are of Israel:

Rom.15.4.bsb: For everything that was written in the past was written for our instruction, so that through endurance and the encouragement of the Scriptures, we might have hope.
Rom.15.4.kjv: For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.

Rom.3.30.bsb: since there is only one God, who will justify the circumcised by faith and the uncircumcised through that same faith.
Rom.3.30.kjv: Seeing it is one God, which shall justify the circumcision by faith, and uncircumcision through faith.

Rom.3.31.bsb: Do we, then, nullify the law by this faith? Certainly not! Instead, we uphold the law.
Rom.3.31.kjv: Do we then make void the law through faith? God forbid: yea, we establish the law.

Rom.11.6.bsb: And if it is by grace, then it is no longer by works. Otherwise, grace would no longer be grace.
Rom.11.6.kjv: And if by grace, then is it no more of works: otherwise grace is no more grace. But if it be of works, then is it no more grace: otherwise work is no more work.

Rom.16.5.bsb: Greet also the church that meets at their house. Greet my beloved Epenetus, who was the first convert to Christ in the province of Asia.
Rom.16.5.kjv: Likewise greet the church that is in their house. Salute my wellbeloved Epenetus, who is the firstfruits of Achaia unto Christ.

Rom.1.13.bsb: I do not want you to be unaware, brothers, how often I planned to come to you (but have been prevented from visiting until now), in order that I might have a harvest among you, just as I have had among the other Gentiles.
Rom.1.13.kjv: Now I would not have you ignorant, brethren, that oftentimes I purposed to come unto you, (but was let hitherto,) that I might have some fruit among you also, even as among other Gentiles.

Rom.14.5.bsb: One person regards a certain day above the others, while someone else considers every day alike. Each one should be fully convinced in his own mind.
Rom.14.5.kjv: One man esteemeth one day above another: another esteemeth every day alike. Let every man be fully persuaded in his own mind.

Rom.11.24.bsb: For if you were cut from a wild olive tree, and contrary to nature were grafted into one that is cultivated, how much more readily will these, the natural branches, be grafted into their own olive tree!
Rom.11.24.kjv: For if thou wert cut out of the olive tree which is wild by nature, and wert graffed contrary to nature into a good olive tree: how much more shall these, which be the natural branches, be graffed into their own olive tree?

Rom.11.14.bsb: in the hope that I may provoke my own people to jealousy and save some of them.
Rom.11.14.kjv: If by any means I may provoke to emulation them which are my flesh, and might save some of them.

Rom.15.6.bsb: so that with one mind and one voice you may glorify the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.
Rom.15.6.kjv: That ye may with one mind and one mouth glorify God, even the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.

Rom.15.33.bsb: The God of peace be with all of you. Amen.
Rom.15.33.kjv: Now the God of peace be with you all. Amen.

Rom.15.17.bsb: Therefore I exult in Christ Jesus in my service to God.
Rom.15.17.kjv: I have therefore whereof I may glory through Jesus Christ in those things which pertain to God.

Rom.14.22.bsb: Keep your belief about such matters between yourself and God. Blessed is the one who does not condemn himself by what he approves.
Rom.14.22.kjv: Hast thou faith? have it to thyself before God. Happy is he that condemneth not himself in that thing which he alloweth.

Rom.1.15.bsb: That is why I am so eager to preach the gospel also to you who are in Rome.
Rom.1.15.kjv: So, as much as in me is, I am ready to preach the gospel to you that are at Rome also.

Rom.14.15.bsb: If your brother is distressed by what you eat, you are no longer acting in love. Do not by your eating destroy your brother, for whom Christ died.
Rom.14.15.kjv: But if thy brother be grieved with thy meat, now walkest thou not charitably. Destroy not him with thy meat, for whom Christ died.

Rom.1.11.bsb: For I long to see you so that I may impart to you some spiritual gift to strengthen you,
Rom.1.11.kjv: For I long to see you, that I may impart unto you some spiritual gift, to the end ye may be established;

Rom.7.12.bsb: So then, the law is holy, and the commandment is holy, righteous, and good.
Rom.7.12.kjv: Wherefore the law is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good.

Rom.15.7.bsb: Accept one another, then, just as Christ accepted you, in order to bring glory to God.
Rom.15.7.kjv: Wherefore receive ye one another, as Christ also received us to the glory of God.

Rom.2.25.bsb: Circumcision has value if you observe the law, but if you break the law, your circumcision has become uncircumcision.
Rom.2.25.kjv: For circumcision verily profiteth, if thou keep the law: but if thou be a breaker of the law, thy circumcision is made uncircumcision.

Rom.2.26.bsb: If a man who is not circumcised keeps the requirements of the law, will not his uncircumcision be regarded as circumcision?
Rom.2.26.kjv: Therefore if the uncircumcision keep the righteousness of the law, shall not his uncircumcision be counted for circumcision?

Rom.10.15.bsb: And how can they preach unless they are sent? As it is written: “How beautiful are the feet of those who bring good news!”
Rom.10.15.kjv: And how shall they preach, except they be sent? as it is written, How beautiful are the feet of them that preach the gospel of peace, and bring glad tidings of good things!

Rom.14.20.bsb: Do not destroy the work of God for the sake of food. All food is clean, but it is wrong for a man to let his eating be a stumbling block.
Rom.14.20.kjv: For meat destroy not the work of God. All things indeed are pure; but it is evil for that man who eateth with offence.

Rom.11.10.bsb: May their eyes be darkened so they cannot see, and their backs be bent forever.”
Rom.11.10.kjv: Let their eyes be darkened, that they may not see, and bow down their back alway.

Rom.1.12.bsb: that is, that you and I may be mutually encouraged by each other’s faith.
Rom.1.12.kjv: That is, that I may be comforted together with you by the mutual faith both of you and me.

Rom.14.9.bsb: For this reason Christ died and returned to life, that He might be the Lord of both the dead and the living.
Rom.14.9.kjv: For to this end Christ both died, and rose, and revived, that he might be Lord both of the dead and living.

Rom.2.3.bsb: So when you, O man, pass judgment on others, yet do the same things, do you think you will escape God’s judgment?
Rom.2.3.kjv: And thinkest thou this, O man, that judgest them which do such things, and doest the same, that thou shalt escape the judgment of God?

Rom.15.28.bsb: So after I have completed this service and have safely delivered this bounty to them, I will set off to Spain by way of you.
Rom.15.28.kjv: When therefore I have performed this, and have sealed to them this fruit, I will come by you into Spain.

Rom.11.13.bsb: I am speaking to you Gentiles. Inasmuch as I am the apostle to the Gentiles, I magnify my ministry
Rom.11.13.kjv: For I speak to you Gentiles, inasmuch as I am the apostle of the Gentiles, I magnify mine office:

Rom.10.14.bsb: How then can they call on the One in whom they have not believed? And how can they believe in the One of whom they have not heard? And how can they hear without someone to preach?
Rom.10.14.kjv: How then shall they call on him in whom they have not believed? and how shall they believe in him of whom they have not heard? and how shall they hear without a preacher?

Rom.14.13.bsb: Therefore let us stop judging one another. Instead, make up your mind not to put any stumbling block or obstacle in your brother’s way.
Rom.14.13.kjv: Let us not therefore judge one another any more: but judge this rather, that no man put a stumblingblock or an occasion to fall in his brother’s way.

Rom.2.28.bsb: A man is not a Jew because he is one outwardly, nor is circumcision only outward and physical.
Rom.2.28.kjv: For he is not a Jew, which is one outwardly; neither is that circumcision, which is outward in the flesh:

Rom.11.21.bsb: For if God did not spare the natural branches, He will certainly not spare you either.
Rom.11.21.kjv: For if God spared not the natural branches, take heed lest he also spare not thee.

Rom.3.8.bsb: Why not say, as some slanderously claim that we say, “Let us do evil that good may result”? Their condemnation is deserved!
Rom.3.8.kjv: And not rather, (as we be slanderously reported, and as some affirm that we say,) Let us do evil, that good may come? whose damnation is just.

Rom.5.7.bsb: Very rarely will anyone die for a righteous man, though for a good man someone might possibly dare to die.
Rom.5.7.kjv: For scarcely for a righteous man will one die: yet peradventure for a good man some would even dare to die.

Rom.16.16.bsb: Greet one another with a holy kiss. All the churches of Christ send you greetings.
Rom.16.16.kjv: Salute one another with an holy kiss. The churches of Christ salute you.
